title: sdks: unify auth/retries and streaming ergonomics across Python/TS/Go; parity fixes & v1.182.0 bump
author: Maya Chen
body: Summary: This PR unifies auth and retry behavior across the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs, stabilizes streaming ergonomics (parity on callbacks/promises/chan), applies several small parity fixes discovered during cross-language testing, and bumps SDK package versions to v1.182.0. Motivation: Historically each SDK evolved independently which led to subtle differences in credential refresh semantics, retry backoff defaults, and streaming user APIs. This caused integration friction for customers moving between languages and made our examples/documentation harder to maintain. Changes include: 1) centralizing auth token refresh semantics so SDKs refresh proactively at the same threshold and surface consistent errors; 2) consolidating retry policy defaults (max_retries=3, exponential backoff with jitter, idempotency heuristics) and exposing the same ergonomic override surface in each SDK; 3) aligning streaming APIs: Python yields async generator + sync iterator, TS supports both async iterator and callback-based streamHandler, Go exposes a channel-based stream and helper wrapper; 4) parity fixes: ensure streaming close semantics flush KV cache, fix header propagation in Go proxy transport, unify User-Agent across SDKs; 5) package version bumps and CHANGELOG entries. Testing: Local and CI test matrix ran across py 3.9/3.11, node 18/20, go 1.20/1.21. Added interoperability smoke tests that instantiate a conversation in one language and validate token count / final output when a second language fetches the same model with the same prompt (ensures retry/auth parity). Rollout plan: merge to main, publish SDK packages in staged order (python -> typescript -> go) and coordinate with docs release. Backwards compatibility: default behaviors are carefully preserved; most changes are bugfixes and ergonomics improvements. Callouts: Go streaming added a convenience wrapper that is opt-in; no breaking changes expected. Checklist: [x] Tests added/updated; [x] CHANGELOG updated; [x] Docs notes added for streaming ergonomics; [x] Version bumps staged. See linked Linear tasks ENG-8841 for cross-SDK design and ENG-8899 for test harness work.
commits: 7a1f3d4  unify: extract auth token refresher into shared contract
ab8c9e2  sdk(python): implement unified retry policy and add interoperability smoke test
b4c2d1f  sdk(ts): align streaming handler with python ergonomics; add docs examples
c3d4e5a  sdk(go): add channel wrapper for streaming and fix header propagation bug
d9e0f12  ci: add matrix job for cross-language smoke tests
e6f7a89  release: bump python/typescript/go SDK versions to v1.182.0 and update CHANGELOG
review_comments: Arjun Patel: Left a few nits on the Python retry wrapper. Can we expose a typed RetryPolicy object rather than positional args? Also confirm that the proactive token refresh window is configurable per-client.

Maya Chen: Thanks Arjun, addressed by adding RetryPolicy dataclass and exposing client.retry_policy in Python. Token refresh window moved to client.auth.refresh_window_seconds with default 60s. Updated tests. PTAL.

Sofia Martinez: TS changes look good overall. Two requests: (1) document the streaming callback vs async iterator difference in the examples, (2) ensure package.json exports remain compatible for ESM/CJS. CI failed on node 18 with a module resolution error.
Maya Chen: Fixed the TS exports issue (conditional exports) and pushed a patch. CI reran and passed. Added doc examples addressing callback vs iterator.

Dmitri Ivanov: Go streaming wrapper is clean. One concern: header propagation fix touches the proxy transport. Please add a unit test that simulates proxy adding extra headers and assert they get forwarded. Also prefer context.Context usage in wrapper for cancellation.
Maya Chen: Added unit test for proxy header propagation and refactored streaming wrapper to accept context.Context for graceful cancellation. All reviewers approved after final CI run.
release_notes: SDKs: unify auth token refresh and retry defaults across Python/TypeScript/Go; improved streaming ergonomics and parity; fixed header propagation bug in Go proxy transport; added cross-language interoperability smoke tests; bumped SDK versions to v1.182.0.
